ei.title: Two Heroes Who Fought a Deadly Disease
ei.subject: 영어2

fullPassage: One evening in late November 1932, a bitterly cold wind blows fiercely as two figures emerge from a laboratory. Darkness begins to fall as they set out into a world of failed banks, collapsed industry, and widespread despair — a world ruined by three years of the Great Depression. The workday has come to an end, but for Pearl Kendrick and Grace Eldering, a different kind of work is about to begin. They are on their way to visit the homes of children suffering from a deadly disease called pertussis*. The two women go from home to home collecting samples from the sick children by the faint light of their lamps. They listen to the tragic stories of desperate and unemployed parents as the children, coughing uncontrollably and struggling to breathe, barely hold on to life. Pertussis is a bacterial disease characterized by serious coughing, breathing difficulties, and the high-pitched “whooping” sound that people with the disease make as they try to breathe in. Because of this distinct sound, people started to call the disease “whooping cough.” For a long time, this terrible illness was one of the greatest terrors of families with young children, because babies who contracted it had a high chance of dying. In the 1930s, an average of 6,000 people died of whooping cough in the United States each year. Ninety-five percent of them were children under five years of age. The cause of the disease had been identified in 1906, but the vaccines that had been developed were ineffective. Scientists and researchers worked for more than 20 years to produce an effective one, but their efforts were fruitless — until Kendrick and Eldering came along. Pearl Kendrick studied bacteriology in university and was recruited by the Michigan Department of Health in 1920. It was there that she met fellow bacteriologist Grace Eldering. The two quickly bonded, and in 1932 they started working together on a vaccine for whooping cough. Personal experience served as motivation for both of them, as they had each survived whooping cough as children themselves and remembered the severe pain of the disease. Both scientists were also eager to promote children’s health. Unfortunately, research funding was extremely limited due to the Great Depression. Also, Kendrick and Eldering had to develop the vaccine as a side project. It was like having a second job for which they never received any payment. Still, when they finished their normal duties each day, they would get started on the work that they were enthusiastic about. The difficulties they faced did not stop them from persisting toward their goal. They did not do the work to make extra money; instead, they worked to relieve the suffering of innocent children and their families. They began the process of developing their vaccine by gathering samples of the bacteria that cause whooping cough. To support them, local doctors and nurses provided “cough plates” from their patients. The patients coughed onto a petri dish*, which was then put into an incubator. This allowed the bacteria to grow into colonies that Kendrick and Eldering could analyze. When they collected samples on their own, they would go to the homes of sick children. Each time, they were reminded once again of the dreadful suffering caused by the disease. The sight of these innocent young victims coughing and struggling to breathe was a powerful reminder of the urgent need for an effective vaccine. Kendrick and Eldering spent many long nights studying the bacteria and finally produced a potential vaccine. Before they performed any clinical trials, though, they had to be certain that it would not have any negative side effects on the subjects. They ran many laboratory tests, and they even injected it into themselves to confirm that it was safe. From 1934 to 1935, they conducted their first field test with 1,592 children. In the group of 712 vaccinated children, only four developed whooping cough, and none of these cases were serious. Despite the apparent success of the vaccine, Kendrick and Eldering wanted further confirmation of its effectiveness. They became determined to expand their research and run more tests with larger groups of children. However, they were unable to proceed because they were facing a severe lack of funds. With thousands of children continuing to suffer from the disease, they found themselves in a desperate situation. Luckily, they got help from an unexpected figure. In 1936, First Lady Eleanor Roosevelt herself visited the laboratory and saw with her own eyes the efforts that Kendrick and Eldering were making in their battle against whooping cough. Eleanor Roosevelt, whose husband suffered from polio*, was interested in fighting infectious diseases. She spent time with the women and came to realize the enormous importance of their work. With her help, Kendrick and Eldering were able to secure enough funding to conduct a large-scale trial. By 1937, Kendrick and Eldering were able to include more than 4,200 children in their trial. Just as in their first field test, the vaccinated group demonstrated a high level of immunity against the disease. The scientific community was amazed at the results, and, in 1940, the vaccine started being distributed all across the United States. Four years later, it was added to the American Medical Association’s list of recommended immunizations, and soon after, there was a dramatic decline in whooping cough infections. In the mid-1970s, the number of annual deaths caused by whooping cough, which had reached 7,518 in 1934, dropped to under 10. Kendrick and Eldering were often told that they could have become very wealthy if they had patented their vaccine. However, they replied that it had not been created by them alone, but with the help of many others. They also avoided personal interviews, not wanting to reveal the great contribution they had made. They said that they had genuinely enjoyed the challenge of creating the vaccine, so the excessive praise that they received made them uncomfortable. In the end, knowing that so many lives were being saved thanks to their hard work was enough of a reward for these remarkable and modest heroes.

questions.passage: They listen to the tragic stories of desperate and unemployed parents as the children, coughing uncontrollably and ①<u>struggling</u> to breathe, barely hold on to life. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ makes → make: 관계사절의 주어가 복수(people)이므로 복수 동사 make
det.analysis:
① struggling: 'coughing uncontrollably and struggling to breathe'에서 앞의 coughing과 and로 나란히 이어지는 분사(-ing)라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② characterized: 'a bacterial disease characterized by ~'는 '~을 특징으로 하는 질병'이라는 뜻으로, 질병이 특징지어지는 대상이라 과거분사(p.p.)가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ makes → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'the sound that people with the disease makes'에서 관계대명사 that이 이끄는 절의 주어는 people(사람들, 복수)이에요. 복수 주어에는 makes가 아니라 make를 써야 해요. 중간에 끼어든 'with the disease'에 속지 마세요. ❌ makes는 틀림 ←정답

④ died: 'an average of 6,000 people died'에서 1930년대(과거) 이야기라 과거 시제 died가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 관계사절 주어가 복수(people)면 동사도 복수(make). 사이에 낀 수식어구에 속지 않기

questions.passage: The cause of the disease ①<u>had been identified</u> in 1906, but the vaccines that had been developed ②<u>was ineffective</u>.  Scientists and researchers worked for more than 20 years ③<u>to produce</u> an effective one, but their efforts were fruitless — until Kendrick and Eldering came along.  Pearl Kendrick studied bacteriology in university and was recruited by the Michigan Department of Health in 1920.  It was there that she ④<u>met</u> fellow bacteriologist Grace Eldering.  The two quickly bonded, and in 1932 they started working together on a vaccine for whooping cough.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② was → were: 주어가 the vaccines(복수)이므로 복수 동사 were
det.analysis:
① had been identified: 'The cause ~ had been identified in 1906'은 '1906년에 (이미) 밝혀졌다'로, 과거의 어느 시점보다 더 앞선 일을 나타내는 과거완료 수동태라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② was ineffective → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'the vaccines that had been developed were ineffective'에서 진짜 주어는 the vaccines(백신들, 복수)예요. 복수 주어에는 was가 아니라 were를 써야 해요. ❌ was ineffective는 틀림 ←정답

③ to produce: 'worked ~ to produce an effective one'은 '효과적인 것을 만들기 위해 애썼다'로, 목적을 나타내는 to부정사라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ met: 'It was there that she met ~'은 과거에 만난 일이라 과거형 met이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 복수 주어(the vaccines)에는 복수 동사 were

questions.passage: Just as in their first field test, the vaccinated group demonstrated a high level of immunity against the disease. Four years later, it was added to the American Medical Association’s list of ②<u>recommended</u> immunizations, and soon after, ③<u>there was</u> a dramatic decline in whooping cough infections. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① distributed → being distributed: 'start + 동명사'이고 백신은 '배포되는' 대상이라 수동 동명사 being distributed
det.analysis:
① distributed → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'the vaccine started ___ all across the United States'에서 백신은 스스로 배포하는 게 아니라 '배포되는' 대상이에요. start 뒤에 동명사를 쓰되 수동의 의미라 being distributed(배포되는 것)로 써야 해요. distributed 하나만 쓰면 틀려요. ❌ distributed는 틀림 ←정답

② recommended: 'list of recommended immunizations'는 '권장되는 예방접종 목록'으로, 명사를 꾸미는 과거분사라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ there was: 'there was a dramatic decline'에서 뒤의 주어가 a dramatic decline(단수)이라 단수 was가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ which had reached: 'whooping cough, which had reached 7,518 in 1934'는 콤마 뒤에서 앞 명사를 받아 설명하는 계속적 용법 관계대명사라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: start + being + p.p.: 시작되는 동작이 '수동(배포되는)'일 때 being distributed

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ cheerful → tragic: 절박하고 실직한 부모들의 '비극적인' 이야기
det.analysis:
① fiercely: 몹시 차가운 바람이 '맹렬히' 분다는 문맥에 적절해요. ✅ 적절

② despair: 무너진 은행과 산업, '널리 퍼진 절망'이라는 대공황의 배경 묘사에 적절해요. ✅ 적절

③ deadly: 아이들이 앓는 '치명적인' 질병(pertussis)이라는 문맥에 적절해요. ✅ 적절

④ cheerful → 여기가 정답(부적절한 곳)! 원문은 'the tragic stories of desperate and unemployed parents'로 '절박하고 실직한 부모들의 비극적인 이야기'예요. 절망적인 상황이니 '비극적인(tragic)'이 맞는데, cheerful(즐거운)은 정반대라 문맥에 안 맞아요. ❌ 부적절 ←정답
det.tip: desperate·unemployed(절박한·실직한)와 어울리는 것은 tragic(비극적인)

questions.passage: Despite the ①<u>apparent</u> success of the vaccine, Kendrick and Eldering wanted further confirmation of its effectiveness.  They became determined to ②<u>limit</u> their research and run more tests with larger groups of children.  However, they were ③<u>unable</u> to proceed because they were facing a severe lack of funds.  With thousands of children continuing to suffer from the disease, they found themselves in a ④<u>desperate situation</u>.  Luckily, they got help from an unexpected figure.  In 1936, First Lady Eleanor Roosevelt herself visited the laboratory and saw with her own eyes the efforts that Kendrick and Eldering were making in their battle against whooping cough.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② limit → expand: 더 많은 시험을 하려고 연구를 '확장'하기로 결심함
det.analysis:
① apparent: '백신의 명백한(apparent) 성공에도 불구하고'라는 문맥에 적절해요. ✅ 적절

② limit → 여기가 정답(부적절한 곳)! 원문은 'They became determined to expand their research and run more tests with larger groups'로, 더 많은 시험을 더 큰 집단으로 하려고 연구를 '확장하기로(expand)' 결심한 거예요. 뒤에 'run more tests'가 이어지니 limit(제한하다)은 정반대라 안 맞아요. ❌ 부적절 ←정답

③ unable: 자금 부족으로 진행'할 수 없었다(unable)'는 문맥에 적절해요. ✅ 적절

④ desperate situation: 수많은 아이들이 계속 고통받는 '절박한 상황'이라는 문맥에 적절해요. ✅ 적절
det.tip: 뒤에 run more tests(더 많은 시험)가 이어지니 expand(확장하다), limit(제한하다) 아님

questions.passage: They began the process of developing their vaccine by gathering samples of the bacteria that cause whooping cough.  To support them, local doctors and nurses provided “__________” from their patients.  The patients coughed onto a petri dish*, which was then put into an incubator.  This allowed the bacteria to grow into colonies that Kendrick and Eldering could analyze.  When they collected samples on their own, they would go to the homes of sick children.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① cough plates(기침 배양판): 환자가 접시에 기침을 하면 배양기에 넣어 세균을 키움
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'To support them, local doctors and nurses provided ___ from their patients. The patients coughed onto a petri dish, which was then put into an incubator.'(지역 의사와 간호사가 환자들에게서 ___을 제공했다. 환자들이 페트리 접시에 기침을 하면 배양기에 넣었다). 환자가 '기침을 해서' 세균을 얻는 것이므로 빈칸은 '기침 배양판(cough plates)'이 되어야 해요.

✅ ① cough plates(기침 배양판): 환자가 접시에 기침을 해 세균을 모은다는 뒤 문장과 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ② blood samples(혈액 샘플): 기침을 접시에 하는 방식과 맞지 않아요.

❌ ③ written reports(작성된 보고서): 세균 표본을 얻는 방법과 무관해요.

❌ ④ food supplies(식량): 문맥과 전혀 무관해요.
det.tip: 환자가 기침을 접시에 함(coughed onto a petri dish) → cough plates(기침 배양판)

Kendrick and Eldering spent many long nights studying the bacteria and finally produced a potential vaccine. In the group of 712 vaccinated children, only four developed whooping cough, and none of these cases were serious.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ③ negative side effects(부정적인 부작용): 임상시험 전 안전성 확인을 위해 부작용이 없는지 확실히 해야 함
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'Before they performed any clinical trials, they had to be certain that it would not have any ___ on the subjects. They ran many laboratory tests, and they even injected it into themselves to confirm that it was safe.'(임상시험 전에, 그들은 백신이 피험자에게 어떤 ___도 없을 것이라고 확신해야 했다). 뒤에 '안전한지 확인했다'가 이어지므로 빈칸은 '부정적인 부작용'이 되어야 해요.

❌ ① financial problems(재정 문제): 피험자에게 미치는 안전성 문제가 아니에요.

❌ ② legal restrictions(법적 제약): 백신의 안전성과 무관해요.

✅ ③ negative side effects(부정적인 부작용): '안전한지 확인했다(confirm that it was safe)'는 뒤 문장과 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ④ time limits(시간 제한): 부작용·안전성 문맥과 무관해요.
det.tip: confirm that it was safe(안전 확인)라는 단서 → negative side effects(부정적 부작용)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 백일해의 특성과 초기 대응.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 본문 'Ninety-five percent of them were children under five years of age'에서 사망자의 95%는 5세 미만 아이들이었으므로 '노인'은 불일치

det.korean: 첫 현장 시험과 그 이후.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 본문 'they had to be certain that it would not have any negative side effects'와 일치

❌ ② 본문 'From 1934 to 1935, they conducted their first field test'와 일치

questions.passage: One evening in late November 1932, a bitterly cold wind blows fiercely as two figures emerge from a laboratory.  Darkness begins to fall as they set out into a world of failed banks, collapsed industry, and widespread despair — a world ruined by three years of the Great Depression.  The workday has come to an end, but for Pearl Kendrick and Grace Eldering, a different kind of work is about to begin.  They are on their way to visit the homes of children suffering from a deadly disease called pertussis*.  The two women go from home to home collecting samples from the sick children by the faint light of their lamps.  They listen to the tragic stories of desperate and unemployed parents as the children, coughing uncontrollably and struggling to breathe, barely hold on to life.  Pertussis is a bacterial disease characterized by serious coughing, breathing difficulties, and the high-pitched “whooping” sound that people with the disease make as they try to breathe in.  Because of this distinct sound, people started to call the disease “whooping cough.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ④ the help of many others(많은 사람들의 도움): 백신은 그들만이 아니라 여러 사람의 도움으로 만들어짐
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'they replied that it had not been created by them alone, but with ___'(그것은 그들만의 힘으로 만들어진 것이 아니라 ___으로 만들어졌다고 답했다). 'not A but B(A가 아니라 B)' 구조에서 'them alone(그들만)'과 대비되는 것은 '많은 사람들의 도움'이 되어야 해요.

❌ ① a large sum of money(많은 돈): 이들은 돈을 위해 일하지 않았어요.

❌ ② the latest technology(최신 기술): 본문에 언급되지 않아요.

❌ ③ years of careful study(수년간의 연구): 겸손하게 '남들의 도움'을 강조하는 흐름과 어긋나요.

✅ ④ the help of many others(많은 사람들의 도움): 'not by them alone(그들만이 아니라)'과 대비되어 딱 맞아요 ←정답
det.tip: not by them alone but with ___ : them alone과 대비되는 the help of many others

questions.passage: Pearl Kendrick studied bacteriology in university and was recruited by the Michigan Department of Health in 1920.  It was there that she met fellow bacteriologist Grace Eldering.  The two quickly bonded, and in 1932 __________ for whooping cough.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"그들은 함께 백신 개발 작업을 시작했다." (7단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) a, on, started, they, together, vaccine, working 을 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 7단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: they started working together on a vaccine
det.analysis:
'그들은 시작했다'가 핵심이라 '주어(they) + 동사(started)'로 시작해요.

동사 start는 뒤에 동명사(-ing)를 목적어로 쓸 수 있어요: started + working(작업하는 것을 시작했다).

'함께'는 부사 together로 동사 뒤에 놓아요: working + together.

무엇에 대한 작업인지는 전치사 on으로 이어요: on + a + vaccine(백신에 대해).

순서대로 놓으면 they / started / working / together / on / a / vaccine.
det.tip: start + 동명사(working) / work on ~ (~에 대한 작업을 하다)

questions.wa: they started working together on a vaccine
accept: they started working together on a vaccine

questions.passage: Still, when they finished their normal duties each day, they would get started on the work that they were enthusiastic about.  The difficulties they faced did not stop them from ①<u>to persist</u> toward their goal.  They did not do the work to make extra money; instead, they worked to relieve the suffering of innocent children and their families.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①은 어법상 틀렸다. 어법에 맞게 올바른 형태로 고쳐 쓰시오. (한 단어, 영어로)

det.korean: to persist → persisting: 전치사 from 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)를 써야 하므로 persisting
det.analysis:
밑줄이 있는 문장은 'The difficulties they faced did not stop them from ①<u>to persist</u> toward their goal.'이에요. '그들이 겪은 어려움도 그들이 목표를 향해 나아가는 것을 막지 못했다'라는 뜻이에요.

여기서 'stop A from B(A가 B하는 것을 막다)'라는 표현이 쓰였어요. 이때 from은 전치사예요.

전치사 뒤에는 반드시 동명사(-ing)를 써야 해요. 그래서 to persist(to부정사)가 아니라 persisting(동명사)으로 고쳐야 맞아요.

정답은 persisting이에요.
det.tip: stop A from -ing (A가 ~하는 것을 막다): 전치사 from 뒤에는 동명사 persisting

questions.passage: In the mid-1970s, the number of annual deaths caused by whooping cough, which had reached 7,518 in 1934, dropped to under 10.  Kendrick and Eldering were often told that __________.  However, they replied that it had not been created by them alone, but with the help of many others.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"그들이 백신에 특허를 냈더라면 그들은 매우 부유해질 수도 있었을 것이다." (12단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) become, could, had, have, if, patented, their, they, they, vaccine, very, wealthy 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 12단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: they could have become very wealthy if they had patented their vaccine
det.analysis:
'~했더라면 ~했을 것이다'라는 과거 사실의 반대를 나타내는 가정법 과거완료예요.

주절(결과)은 '조동사 could + have + 과거분사(become)' 형태로 써요: they + could + have + become + very + wealthy(그들은 매우 부유해질 수도 있었다).

if절(조건)은 'if + 주어 + had + 과거분사(patented)' 형태로 써요: if + they + had + patented + their + vaccine(그들이 백신에 특허를 냈더라면).

순서대로 이으면 they / could / have / become / very / wealthy / if / they / had / patented / their / vaccine.
det.tip: 가정법 과거완료: 주절 could have p.p. + if절 had p.p.

questions.wa: they could have become very wealthy if they had patented their vaccine
accept: they could have become very wealthy if they had patented their vaccine

questions.passage: They did not do the work to make extra money; instead, they worked to relieve the suffering of innocent children and their families.  __________ by gathering samples of the bacteria that cause whooping cough.  To support them, local doctors and nurses provided “cough plates” from their patients.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.
"그들은 자신들의 백신을 개발하는 과정을 시작했다."

[ began / developing / of / process / the / their / They / vaccine ] (8단어) (영어로)

det.korean: They began the process of developing their vaccine
det.analysis:
'그들은 과정을 시작했다'를 영어 어순으로 놓아요.

먼저 주어와 동사: They(그들은) + began(시작했다).

무엇을 시작했는가 하면 목적어 the process(그 과정)예요: the + process.

어떤 과정인지는 전치사 of로 이어요. of 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)를 쓰므로 of developing(개발하는)이 되고, 그 뒤에 their vaccine(자신들의 백신)을 붙여요: of + developing + their + vaccine.

순서대로 이으면 They / began / the / process / of / developing / their / vaccine.
det.tip: the process of + 동명사(developing): ~하는 과정

questions.wa: They began the process of developing their vaccine
accept: They began the process of developing their vaccine

questions.passage: Kendrick and Eldering were often told that they could have become very wealthy if they had patented their vaccine.  However, they replied that __________, but with the help of many others.  They also avoided personal interviews, not wanting to reveal the great contribution they had made.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"그것은 그들만의 힘으로 만들어진 것이 아니었다." (8단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) alone, been, by, created, had, it, not, them 을 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 8단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: it had not been created by them alone
det.analysis:
'그것은 만들어진 것이 아니었다'는 '~되다'라는 수동의 뜻이고, 앞선 시점의 일이라 과거완료 수동태로 써요.

과거완료 수동태 부정은 'had + not + been + 과거분사(created)' 형태예요: it + had + not + been + created(그것은 만들어지지 않았다).

'그들에 의해'는 행위자를 나타내는 'by + 목적격'으로 쓰고, '그들만으로'라는 뜻의 alone을 뒤에 붙여요: by + them + alone.

순서대로 이으면 it / had / not / been / created / by / them / alone.
det.tip: 과거완료 수동태 부정: had not been + 과거분사(created) / by them alone(그들만의 힘으로)

questions.wa: it had not been created by them alone
accept: it had not been created by them alone
